messages:
melissa: Noticed EU canary (console v2) getting very choppy when opening Metrics. Charts hang ~3-7s and main thread shows large JS parse spikes.
jorge: I can repro on my canary session. Network waterfall shows a burst of identical chunk GETs and a flurry of small prefetch XHRs.
priya: any recent policy/rollout changes? We tweaked the prefetch quota router last Tuesday.
sasha: telemetry sampling was nudged up on canary yesterday (devex run). that makes more sessions hit the telemetry-proxy path and it marks sessions for aggressive prefetch.
melissa: so sampler + routing change -> more inlined telemetry + earlier prefetch activity -> parse storms?
dan: plausible. also saw KV cache churn around the same window which could amplify cold fetches.
jorge: snippet from my devtools:
```
GET /static/widget/heatmap.chunk.js 200 110ms
GET /static/widget/heatmap.chunk.js 200 112ms
GET /kv/prefix?key=heatmap.v2 MISS 0.0ms
GET /static/widget/legend.chunk.js 200 90ms
```
jorge: looks like duplicate fetches within 5-10ms, no affinity to single KV node so TTL/eviction makes them cold.
sasha: telemetry client is being inlined earlier due to sampling initialization during app bootstrap. that bumps parse time and triggers prefetch earlier than before.
melissa: immediate triage: can we patch a small client-side debounce before kicking prefetch to collapse concurrent requests?
jorge: tried 250ms debounce locally: duplicate chunk requests disappear and parse spike magnitude reduces by ~70%. perceived open time goes from ~4s -> ~700ms.
priya: good. i'll also roll back the sampler bump on canary to see impact on telemetry volume.
melissa: infra, can we push a tiny debounce flag to canary first?
infra-bot: deploy 5532200025 started by melissa  status: in_progress
dan: medium-term we should add routing policy to classify telemetry-proxied sessions and give them a lower prefetch quota or opt-out. that avoids heavy client prefetch when sampling is high.
sasha: agree. small tradeoff: a handful of cold users get slower initial loads but we avoid wide CPU parse storms.
priya: sampler revert on canary scheduled in 5m. i'll monitor telemetry ingestion and client-side CPU metrics.
jorge: i'll open a tiny PR for debounce + test that ensures duplicate prefetches are merged by request key.
infra-bot: deploy 5532200025 completed  status: success
melissa: post-debounce numbers: median Metrics open time down from ~4.3s to ~750ms on canary. CPU parse time down ~60%.
priya: after sampler revert telemetry events from canary dropped ~68% and prefetch request rate normalized.
dan: KV eviction rate during the incident window was ~3x baseline; after mitigations it's ~35% lower than peak.
melissa: action items:
- emergency: debounce flag live on canary (done)
- revert sampler on canary (priya)
- implement routing-based prefetch opt-out for telemetry-proxied sessions (sasha + jorge)
- add rollout checklist item: coordinate sampling changes with prefetch/routing owners (devex + telemetry + platform) (dan)
jorge: PR #4123 opened for debounce logic and unit tests.
melissa: thanks everyone. leaving canary up while we verify a few more sessions. i'll add a short postmortem note in the incident doc and ping rollout owners. :memo: :thumbsup:
